title: Activation directions shifted both image and text generation
summary: In UniAR, Emu3.5 and Liquid, some activation directions derived from text also changed image outputs, and some image-derived directions changed text. Emotion transferred in both directions more consistently than size or left–right relations. Transfer also depended on model and layer.
ai_technology: UniAR, Emu3.5 and Liquid; activation interventions
organization: Mila and McGill University; Carnegie Mellon University; MIT CSAIL; Northeastern University

source_review.scope: §§3.1–4 and Appendix A.8, including held-out blinded human ratings

evidence.tested: The study perturbed the shared model representations and compared outputs with unperturbed controls for eight concepts. Three reviewers each rated 320 separate randomized output pairs; their majority labels and the automated judge had agreement of κ=0.62.
evidence.unknown: The concept sets include generated examples. The response varies by model, concept and intervention strength, and transferring a direction does not establish that the underlying computations are identical.
evidence.ai_role: Activation directions derived from learned image or text representations were applied to generation in the other modality to measure how it changed.
